passage:
Grandma Chen made the best rice cakes in the family. Everyone loved them, but she never wrote down the recipe.
When she became too old to cook, her grandchildren tried to make the rice cakes. They asked her how much sugar to use. She answered, "Enough." They asked how long to steam them. She said, "Until they look right."
The first rice cakes were too hard. The second were too sweet. After many tries, they finally came close.
Grandma smiled and said, "Now you understand. A recipe is not only numbers. It is practice."
The grandchildren wrote down what they learned, but they also knew that the real recipe had lived in Grandma's hands.
